summary: A corm herb raises pale cups around dark nectar discs after sustained soil wetting. Dawn flowers mark a temporary wet-season opportunity; summer dormancy leaves the meadow open.

links: Seasonal drought makes continuous foliage costly
A buried corm preserves reserves through dormancy
Sustained root-zone wetting permits emergence and flowering
chains.play: Read flowering patches as evidence of recent sustained wetting; harvest starchy corms at the cost of individual plants.
chains.weakness: Brief fog or surface dew cannot trigger a reliable bloom.

plausibility.summary: Local moisture and developmental state govern flowering; blooms do not prove permanent or drinkable groundwater.

analogues.mechanism: An underground corm stores reserves across seasonal shoot dormancy; the analogue concerns storage, not edibility.

chains.trait: Dawn-opening pale cups with dark nectar discs
links: Cream petals contrast with green foliage under scattered daylight
Shallow cups expose nectar and pollen to small flies
Humid, sheltered dawn conditions favour local scent-guided visits
chains.play: Watch inferred hairy flies contact anthers and stigmas; use flowers as nearby landmarks.
chains.weakness: Opaque fog hides distant blooms; cold, wind or rain reduces visitation.
observe: Watch a fly touch the disc.

plausibility.summary: Fly pollination is inferred and must be observable. White petals reflect light; dark centres warm only under suitable sunlight.

analogues.mechanism: Open bowl flowers offer accessible reproductive surfaces to visiting insects; exact colour and dawn timing are fictional adaptations.

poison.signal: Green foliage; cream flowers with dark centres.

gameplay.nest_material: Dry scapes and leaves in small quantities.
gameplay.notes: Corm removal kills that individual. Flowering indicates seasonal soil moisture.

relations.note: Hunts flower visitors; pollination is not obligatory.
Competes in seasonally moist open soil.

generator.trunk: None; slender scapes above buried 30–50 mm corms.

overlay_rules: Six to nine cream petals around a charcoal disc.
Flowers 25–40 mm across; translucent, never luminous.

generator.seasonal: Emergence requires sustained wetting; daily opening follows dawn light and humidity within the 26-hour day.
generator.wind_response: Scapes flex; strong wind suppresses visits.

journal.en: The ground drinks first. Then its little candles open.
journal.es: Primero bebe la tierra. Después abre sus pequeñas velas.

secrets: Adjacent hollows can flower weeks apart when their soils retain water differently.
